name: Kolvex FilterMask FM-9 Particulate Half
description:
A no-frills half-face respirator from Kolvex Industrial Supply, the FM-9 is the standard mask on every Circuit factory floor and transit maintenance corridor. Matte charcoal elastomer body, dual side-mounted grey filter cartridges, and a tight-sealing foam inner gasket. The nose bridge is reinforced with a thin aluminum strip for shaping to fit. Strap is a wide neoprene-analog band.

Most worn FM-9s are decorated with marker tags, sticker residue, or paint overspray from the wearer's job site — an accidental archive of everywhere they've worked.
functionality: Filters fine particulates, chemical vapors, and acid-rain aerosols. Cartridges are rated for 40-hour replacement cycles and are widely available at Circuit supply depots. Clip-tab system allows one-hand cartridge swap.
what_it_says: You work somewhere the air will hurt you, and you've made your peace with it.
story_hooks: A batch of counterfeit FM-9 cartridges is circulating in Circuit — they look identical but filter nothing; someone is making money while workers get sick.
A specific lot number of FM-9s was issued to workers at a facility that officially never existed; finding one is a thread that unravels a corponation cover-up.
A Circuit organizer uses the FM-9's standard issue status as a disguise — every face looks the same when you're all wearing Kolvex.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian half-mask respirator covering nose and mouth, projecting a hardened industrial aesthetic. The rigid matte charcoal body dominates the lower face, creating a stark contrast against skin. Grey cylindrical filter cartridges protrude from both cheeks like mechanical gills. Overall impression is functional, no-nonsense, and distinctly working-class.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight against the face with a secure seal. The wide neoprene-analog band stretches around the back of the head, sitting snug against temples and occipital bone. The aluminum nose bridge allows custom molding for individual fit. Not adjustable beyond initial shaping.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte charcoal elastomer body, grey filter cartridges (activated carbon composite), aluminum nose bridge strip, neoprene-analog head strap, foam inner gasket
physical_description.texture: Smooth matte elastomer exterior with a slight rubbery grip. Filter cartridges have a ridged, cylindrical surface. Foam gasket is soft and slightly tacky against skin. Aluminum bridge is cold and rigid. Visible wear from repeated handling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal grey base with light grey cylindrical filter cartridges. Accent wear: marker tag residue in faded blues and reds, paint overspray in industrial colours (rust orange, slate, chrome silver), sticker adhesive ghosts
physical_description.closures: Single wide neoprene-analog strap with friction-fit elastic tension, no buckles or snaps. Filters cartridge-mount directly into side ports with quarter-turn bayonet fittings.
distinctive_features: Reinforced aluminum nose bridge for custom fitting
Foam inner gasket with visible compression marks
Marker tags and paint overspray from job-site work
Sticker residue and wear patterns indicating heavy use
Wide neoprene strap shows creasing and fatigue
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Standard-issue working class equipment, no luxury affordances.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Circuit factory workers, transit maintenance crews, and site-level industrial workers. Signals time spent in contaminated environments, physical labor, and unglamorous infrastructure work. The accumulated job-site markers become a personal record of employment history.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and marked. Most FM-9s show visible paint overspray, faded marker tags, adhesive residue, and minor elastomer discoloration from sweat and industrial exposure. Filters are regularly replaced; the body persists across years of reuse.
